questions.prompt: What is a Shared Access Signature (SAS)?

options.text: A permanent master key for the whole storage account
A time-limited, scoped token that grants specific permissions to storage data
A type of blob access tier

questions.explanation: A SAS is a time-limited, scoped token (usually in a URL) granting specific permissions. A user-delegation SAS, signed with Entra ID credentials, is preferred over key-based SAS.

questions.prompt: Which are good security practices for Blob storage? Select all that apply.

options.text: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID + RBAC for access
Keep SAS tokens narrowly scoped and short-lived
Use a user-delegation SAS instead of an account-key SAS when possible
Embed account keys directly in application code

questions.explanation: Prefer Entra ID/RBAC; keep SAS scoped and short; prefer user-delegation SAS. Never embed account keys in app code — a leak exposes the whole account.

questions.prompt: Rules that automatically move blobs between tiers or delete them based on age are called ____ management.
questions.explanation: Lifecycle management rules auto-transition blobs between tiers (e.g., to cool/archive) or delete them by age, reducing cost without manual work.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to share a single blob with a read-only SAS.
questions.explanation: Scope permissions to read, set a short expiry, generate the SAS, then share the URL — least privilege and minimal exposure.

questions.prompt: Match each authorization method or feature to its description.

pairs.right: Master key for the whole account (avoid in apps)

questions.explanation: Account keys are all-powerful (avoid in apps); SAS is scoped/temporary; Entra ID + RBAC is most secure; static website hosting serves files from $web.
